anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Optimizer input metadata (row counts, histograms, correlation stats) is stale, missing, or inaccurate, causing systematic cardinality misestimation.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk table and index pages are physically or logically corrupted, breaking key ordering, page links, or heap-to-index consistency.
Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly : Kernel-enforced limits on file handles, shared memory, semaphores, threads, or other OS objects are exhausted, preventing the database from allocating critical resources.

When all three root causes coexist, symptoms intertwine: queries may flip from efficient index plans to full table scans because the optimizer underestimates or overestimates row counts while simultaneously distrusting corrupted indexes and encountering OS errors when attempting to open alternate access paths, spawn parallel workers, or read recovery segments. Estimated-vs-actual row gaps, repeated plan recompilations, and integrity check failures surface alongside sporadic "cannot open file" or "cannot create shared memory" engine errors. Administrators may observe erratic performance spikes, partially missing result sets, and intermittent session or background-worker failures; corruption repair or index rebuild attempts may abort midway due to OS resource denials, leaving objects in even less consistent states.

Causal chain: stale or absent statistics can drive the optimizer to favor access paths that intensively exercise particular indexes or create large temporary workfiles, increasing I/O and handle usage; this added pressure accelerates the exhaustion of OS-level limits. Once limits are hit, critical maintenance tasks—such as automatic page verification, index rebuilds, or statistics refreshes—fail to complete, allowing existing block and index corruptions to persist and spread. Conversely, latent page corruption can trigger repeated plan invalidations and emergency scans that inflate resource consumption, hastening resource-limit breaches and deferring statistics collection that relies on full object scans. The mutual reinforcement of bad statistics, structural corruption, and kernel resource starvation creates a feedback loop that steadily degrades both query correctness and engine availability.

entry.official_description: posix_fallocate(): Failed to preallocate data for file %s, desired size %llu Operating system error number %d - %s. Check that the disk is not full or a disk quota exceeded. Make sure the file system supports this function. Refer to your operating system documentation for operating system error code information.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with file creation, filesystem access, write durability, log persistence, tablespace management, or storage-capacity boundaries.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect filesystem capacity and permissions, verify persistence paths, review log and data placement, and check whether storage latency or write failures are affecting the engine.
